helpPage.title: About TrustDeck

what.title: What is TrustDeck?
what.text: TrustDeck is a trusted third party service for research projects. It manages the identities of study participants, cases, and biosamples and replaces identifying data, such as names, dates of birth, or sample numbers, with pseudonyms. Researchers then work with the pseudonyms, while the identifying data stays protected in TrustDeck.

who.title: Who uses TrustDeck?
who.text: TrustDeck is used by the staff of research projects and trusted third party offices, for example to register participants, create pseudonyms, or look them up.

access.title: How do I get access?
access.text: Anyone can sign in to TrustDeck: either by registering or, if your institution has connected its accounts, with your institutional account. After signing in, however, you do not have any access rights in TrustDeck yet. Permissions must be assigned to you by someone who already has them, usually the principal investigator (PI) of your project. Please contact them to get the permissions you need.

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.text: More information about TrustDeck and how to use it can be found in the documentation.
